TEXT_D:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values and approach
- Principles: Freedom, Fairness, Trust, with a “green thread” through all policies and strong internationalism.
- Funding: Switch ~£5bn/yr from low-priority spend (abolish DTI, scrap ID cards, redirect Child Trust Fund). One tax rise: 50% rate on income over £100,000 to fund scrapping tuition fees, free personal care, and lower local taxes via replacing Council Tax with a fairer Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450). Raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Health
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled, implement Royal Commission.
- Faster diagnosis using all capacity; more evening/weekend scans; publish test waits; train staff to use scanners.
- Free eye/dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; rebuild NHS dentistry.
- Recruit 8,000 doctors, 12,000 nurses, 18,000 therapists; cut central targets, empower local decision-making.
- Personal care plans, stronger mental health rights; end age discrimination.
- Prevention: school nutrition standards, restrict junk-food ads, healthy vending rules; ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore maintenance grants.
- Cut class sizes (infants avg 20; juniors 25) by using Child Trust Fund money; extend 8am–6pm provision; expand Children’s Centres.
- Qualified teachers in core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing; stronger discipline support.
- Better SEN provision; 14–19 diploma blending academic/vocational; equal funding for equivalent courses; invest in college facilities; protect school transport rights.

Crime, liberty, immigration
- 10,000 extra police funded by scrapping ID cards; complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy.
- Community payback; targeted action on binge drinking; rehabilitation and skills in prisons tied to release.
- Create UK Border Force; prosecute terror in mainstream courts; admit intercept evidence; repeal flawed control-order law.
- Fair, faster asylum via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work. Single Equality Act; hate-crime units.

Economy and business
- Fiscal stability with independent NAO scrutiny; ONS independence; rein in irresponsible lending.
- Fairer, simpler taxes; consult on business tax reform; managed economic migration.
- Slash red tape (impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspectorate); small business rate relief (up to £1,500); abolish DTI and redirect funds; legal duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green economy: convert Climate Change Levy to Carbon Tax; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no new nuclear; stronger incentives for clean cars/homes.

Pensions and benefits
- Citizen’s Pension from 75: £109.45 (single), £167.05 (couple), earnings-linked; reduce means-testing. Local Income Tax benefits 8/10 pensioners.
- Maternity Income Guarantee: £170/week for 6 months for first child.
- Reform New Deal; scrap CSA (move to Inland Revenue with tribunal appeals); Winter Fuel Payment for severely disabled; bolster pensions compensation; cut fraud/error; insulation vouchers to cut bills.

Communities, housing, culture
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax.
- 100,000 affordable homes on public land; VAT reform to favour brownfield/renovation; planning permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; protect post offices and universal mail; devolve powers; streamline inspections.
- Waste: 60% household recycling in 7 years; zero-waste goal; climate-conscious planning/building regs.

International, Europe, defence, development
- Opposed Iraq war; support transition and aim to withdraw by UN mandate end; rebuild multilateralism, UN reform, Middle East peace.
- Support EU Constitution via referendum; prepare to join euro when conditions met.
- Armed forces: end overstretch; improve procurement; cut Eurofighter Tranche 3; share burdens via NATO/EU; retain minimum deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms export controls.
- Aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; fairer trade, end dumping; green, sustainable development; lead on climate with “contraction and convergence.”

Rural and environment
- Fair farm prices (duty to trade fairly; Food Trade Inspector); CAP/CFP reform; Marine Act; Animal Welfare Act and Commission; precaution on GM, support organics.

Transport
- Reform rail franchising; restore key upgrades; improve station safety.
- Reward low-emission cars (VED reform); expand congestion charging; long-term national road pricing to replace fuel duty/VED.
- Free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for eligible groups; limit new road-building; boost public transport, rail freight, waterways; per-aircraft aviation charges; oppose new/expanded SE airports; protect lifeline routes.

Better government
- Curb PM powers (War Powers Act), Civil Service Act, stronger Select Committees; predominantly elected second chamber; STV for Commons and local/devolved; votes at 16; devolve quango powers; fair funding across UK.
- Make BBC independent via external regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; create an Environment-Transport-Energy department.

TEXT_C:
Green Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision: Build a sustainable society grounded in social, economic and environmental justice. Reverse privatisation of public services, place peace and human rights at the core of foreign policy, and act decisively on climate change.

Economy
- Tackle inequality with progressive taxation: 50% on income over £50k; 60% over £100k. More corporation tax bands (40% for profits >£1.5m). Increase taxes on unearned wealth; recipient-based, progressive inheritance tax.
- Abolish National Insurance; tax all income uniformly. Pilot Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes on resource use, pollution and waste; include aviation fuel and plastic bags.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; support small businesses and co-ops; oppose joining the euro; reform WTO.
- Create green jobs via renewables, low-carbon transport, zero-waste. Strengthen workers’ rights; reduce working hours. Measure well-being beyond GDP (ISEW/MDP).

Energy and Climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: CO2 cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020, 85% by 2030; develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic VAT and Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax; protect low-income users via tariff reform.
- Target 40% renewable energy by 2020; invest in solar, wind (on/offshore), wave, and biogas; two million small-scale wind systems and two million m² solar by 2010.
- Cut demand: Warmer Homes Act (30% domestic reduction in 10 years); Smart Energy Councils (45% emission cut by 2020).
- Close nuclear as stations reach end-of-life; shift R&D subsidies to renewables; Cabinet post for climate policy.

Welfare
- Phase in a universal Citizen’s Income replacing most means-tested benefits; retain disability/incapacity benefits; integrate housing benefit later.
- Citizen’s Pension: universal, earnings-linked, replaces Pension Credit; initial level at Pension Credit Guarantee.
- Increase child support; simplify systems; expand Sure Start; end Working Time Directive opt-out; move toward 35-hour week.
- Housing: let councils build with sales receipts; support self-build co-ops; drive insulation/efficiency; reform land via LVT.

Health and Education
- Restore NHS principles; end PPPs/foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in healthcare. Abolish prescription charges; free eye tests and dental; support holistic treatments.
- Fund NHS to at least 9% of GNP (~£90bn); consider hypothecated NHS Tax; prioritise prevention and mental health.
- Boost education funding, expand Children’s Centres; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants (align with Citizen’s Income); abolish SATs; introduce individual learning plans.

Transport
- Shift to walking, cycling, public transport, rail freight; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; redirect £30bn from roads to public transport; re-regulate buses.
- Return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Price true motoring costs: extend congestion/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish tax disc; size/pollution-based freight duty; invest in cleaner vehicle R&D.
- Curb aviation: resist airport expansion; ban night flights; EU-wide aviation fuel tax; domestic emissions tax; raise APD; shift short-haul to rail.

Environment, Food, Farming, Animal Welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; 60% domestic recycling by 2010; Zero Waste Agency; eco-taxes on harmful inputs; stronger chemicals regulation.
- Precautionary principle on GM, xenotransplantation, nanotech; oppose TRIPS patents on natural resources.
- End live exports; ban battery eggs (incl. enriched); tougher broiler standards; ban fur; end vivisection.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic by 2012; support local markets. Replace CAP/CFP with support for organics, biodiversity, sustainable incomes. Ban GM food; strengthen supermarket Code with legal watchdog; review OFT.

Crime and Justice
- Prevent crime via urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, visible staff; treat drugs as health issue; oppose ID cards.
- More community policing, local stations, neighbourhood committees; independent complaints system.
- Tough gun controls: prohibit dangerous categories; regulate deactivated guns; single licensing with competence/stability checks; advisory committee.
- Expand restorative justice; strengthen response to hate crimes, violence against women; EU-wide disability rights.

Democracy
- Oppose ID cards. Revive local government with powers (incl. LVT), PR elections, recall (40%) and local referenda (20%).
- PR for Westminster and local councils; elected Lords by PR; regional government by local choice; more powers for Scotland/Wales.
- Written constitution; disestablish Church of England; remove monarchy’s formal roles. Campaign No to proposed EU constitution.

International
- Ethical foreign policy: withdraw from Iraq, support UN peacekeeping; cut defence to EU average; end arms export subsidies; arms trade treaty; decommission nuclear weapons.
- Aid at least 1% GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest; support Tobin tax; equitable carbon trading.
- Reform UN (no permanent Security Council seats, majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Replace/overhaul WTO with General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation and standards.
- Asylum: uphold rights, allow work/benefits, resource decisions, independent appeals; ratify UN migrant workers convention; honour Refugee Convention; review restrictive UK laws.
